steps.title: Distance matters very little
steps.say: You're right that Earth is farther from the Sun in northern summer, about 3% farther. That gap is too small to make a big difference in temperature.

ops.text:
Good question! Earth is about 3%
farther from the Sun in July.

That gap is too small to
cause summer.

steps.title: Tilt decides the heat
steps.say: In northern summer the Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun. Sunlight hits it more directly and the days are longer, so it heats up.

ops.text:
Tilt: sunlight hits the tilted
hemisphere more directly, and days
are longer. That's the real cause.
